title: Kerekes Handshake™ — Universal Claim Schema v1.6
description:
A domain-agnostic schema for anchoring any claim to a forensic vault of primary artifacts. Applicable to professional credentials, trades, consumer goods, real estate, civic accountability, nonprofits, and creative portfolios.

HONEST DISCLOSURE: Self-certification is self-lying. This schema does not prevent fabricated evidence. It makes fabrication more expensive, more detectable via external_verification links, and honestly rated via verification_strength. A PGP signature proves who vouched for the evidence and when — not that the evidence is authentic. The auditor makes the final judgment.

actor.description: The type of entity making the claim.

actor_name.description: Human-readable name of the actor (e.g., 'Joe's Plumbing LLC', 'LG Electronics', 'Jeffrey Kerekes').

domain.description: The system category this claim belongs to (e.g., 'Trades', 'Consumer Goods', 'Civic Systems', 'Real Estate', 'Human Systems', 'Ecological Systems').

claim.description: The specific statement being asserted in plain language.

evidence.description: Primary artifacts supporting the claim. Each artifact should have a matching .txt sidecar for AI extraction (the Text Bridge). Note: the presence of an artifact does not prove its authenticity — see verification_strength.

url.description: Absolute URL to the primary artifact. A matching .txt sidecar should exist at the same path with .txt extension.

description.description: What this specific artifact proves about the claim.

outcome.description: The measurable or verifiable result of the claim.

external_verification.description: Links to third-party public records that independently corroborate the claim. When these point to live government endpoints, they create a Deterministic Collision — if a provided artifact conflicts with the public record, the Handshake fails automatically. This is the path toward apostille-level verification strength.

source.description: Name of the third-party source (e.g., 'Connecticut State Licensing Board', 'congress.gov', 'IRS Form 990 Database').

url.description: Direct URL to the public record or live verification endpoint.

endpoint_type.description: Whether this is a static page (weaker) or a live lookup endpoint (stronger). Live endpoints approach Italy-style QR verification.

verification_strength.description: Honest assessment of how verifiable this claim actually is. Self-certification is self-lying — declare this field honestly. The apostille system took centuries to develop because humans always lied. This field acknowledges that reality while providing a useful signal.

self_declared.description: Actor's honest self-assessment of verification strength on a 1–10 scale. 1–2: self-authored document only. 3–4: third-party authored, no live endpoint. 5–6: third-party corroborated with external link. 7–8: government record with public lookup. 9: live government endpoint verification. 10: Italy-style embedded QR linking to issuing authority.

rationale.description: Plain-language explanation of why this score was chosen. Be honest about limitations.

ai_assessed.description: AI auditor's independent assessment on the same 1–10 scale after reviewing the evidence. Null until assessed. A gap between self_declared and ai_assessed is itself a signal.

ai_rationale.description: AI auditor's explanation for its assessment. Null until assessed.

integrity.description: Cryptographic provenance layer. Identifies who vouched for the evidence and when. A signature proves who signed — not that the underlying evidence is authentic.

signature.description: PGP signature or SHA-256 hash of the manifest.

signed_by.description: Name or PGP fingerprint of the entity signing the manifest.

signed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the manifest was signed.

manifest_url.description: URL to the PGP-signed site_manifest.json.asc file.

examples.claim: Licensed and insured for high-pressure gas lines. License valid through 2026.

evidence.description: Last 5 municipal permit approvals with inspection sign-offs.

examples.outcome: All recent jobs passed municipal inspection on first review.

verification_strength.rationale: License linked to live state lookup. Fabricating a license that matches the live state database would require compromising the state system.

examples.claim: Roof fully replaced in 2022. Permitted and inspected.

evidence.description: Paid roofing contractor invoice dated April 2022.
Municipal building permit with final inspection approval.

examples.outcome: Roof warranty valid through 2042. Final inspection passed 2022-05-03.

verification_strength.rationale: Permit linked to city building department record. Invoice is self-provided with no independent corroboration — a fabricated invoice could match.

examples.claim: Increased sales revenue by 40% over 18 months.

evidence.description: Internal sales report authored by the candidate.

verification_strength.rationale: Self-authored internal document. No external corroboration. This is essentially a resume bullet with a PDF attached. Honest score: low.

examples.claim: Voted in favor of environmental protection legislation in 87% of roll calls over 30 years.

evidence.description: Complete roll-call voting record on environmental bills, 1993–2023.

verification_strength.rationale: Voting records are public federal data. The provided PDF can be verified line-by-line against congress.gov. Cherry-picking specific votes would conflict with the complete public record.
